name: kitex-service
description: Complete Kitex (Thrift) service project: Nacos registration, logging, config, Makefile codegen, CI for GitHub Actions and/or GitLab CI, Dockerfile. Used by `devkit ngs`.

vars.name: Service
vars.description: Service name, lowercase with dashes (e.g. order, order-item)

vars.name: Module
vars.description: Go module path of the new service (e.g. github.com/sezznaw/order)

vars.name: CommonModule
vars.description: Module path of the shared common library. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: CommonVersion
vars.description: Version of common to require. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: IdlRepo
vars.description: Path of the shared IDL project as CI sees it (owner/repo on GitHub, group/project on GitLab). Empty: <owner or group of the service>/idl

vars.name: CI
vars.description: Which CI configuration to generate: github, gitlab, both or none. ngs detects it from module_prefix / idl_repo

vars.name: GoPrivate
vars.description: GOPRIVATE pattern when the organisation's modules are private (empty = public)

vars.name: NacosAddr
vars.description: Nacos server address for the dev config

vars.name: GoVersion
vars.description: Go release (major.minor) for go.mod, the Docker image and GitLab CI; must not be lower than what devkit-common requires. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: KitexVersion
vars.description: Kitex library and tool version. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: ThriftgoVersion
vars.description: thriftgo tool version. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

post_install: if command -v kitex >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v thriftgo >/dev/null 2>&1; then make gen && go mod tidy; else echo '>> kitex/thriftgo not installed. Run: make tools && make gen && go mod tidy'; fi
post_update: go get github.com/cloudwego/kitex@v0.16.3 github.com/sezznaw/devkit-common@v0.3.4 && if grep -rqs --include='*.go' --exclude-dir=kitex_gen 'github.com/sezznaw/devkit-common/log"' .; then echo '>> This service still imports devkit-common/log, which devkit-common v0.3.0 replaced by zlog.'; echo '>> go mod tidy was skipped, it cannot succeed until that code is changed.'; echo '>> Change it as described below, then run: go mod tidy'; else go mod tidy; fi

changes: devkit-common v0.3.4: `service.addr` takes a port. New services get `addr: 8888` in conf/dev.yaml and conf/prod.yaml instead of the quoted `":8888"`. A bare port listens on every network interface, exactly like `":8888"` did; `"host:port"` is still there for listening on one interface only
a bad `service.addr` is reported with the name of the setting and what it accepts, instead of "missing port in address"
action: Nothing has to change: `addr: ":8888"` in your conf/*.yaml keeps working. If you prefer the short form, replace the line with `addr: 8888` (your port) in conf/dev.yaml and conf/prod.yaml.

changes: devkit-common v0.3.3: log sampling says what it left out. Every second in which records were dropped ends with one record per level and message, "zlog: records dropped by sampling" with dropped_msg and dropped, so the size of a flood can be read from the log

conf/README.md has a new section on the three production safeguards of the logger (sampling, max_field_bytes, buffer): what each protects against, what it costs, and when to turn buffer on, which prod.yaml leaves off on purpose

the Docker image no longer contains conf/dev.yaml. A container whose APP_ENV got lost or overridden used to start with the development settings and look healthy: not registered in Nacos, so no caller found it, and logging colored text that a collector cannot parse. Now it refuses to start and names the configuration files there are
action:
Only if you run the image with APP_ENV=dev somewhere, for example in a development cluster: that no longer starts. Give that environment a file of its own:
cp conf/prod.yaml conf/test.yaml      # then adjust it, and deploy with APP_ENV=test
If you had edited the Dockerfile, the new one is next to it as Dockerfile.new; take over the two lines that mention /out/conf.

changes: devkit-common v0.3.2: the "logger configured" record of a starting service says where the values come from that the framework fills in: `service: order (from service.name)`, `env: prod (from APP_ENV)`, or `env: dev (APP_ENV is not set)`. In JSON these remarks, and which settings are defaults, are in "config_notes"

devkit-common v0.3.1: the first record of a starting service, "logger configured", lists the log settings in effect (level, format, stacktrace, sampling, buffer, max_field_bytes, service, env, version, host, output) under the names they have in conf/*.yaml, with "(default)" behind what was not set. It is written whatever the level
a typo in the log settings (for example format: consol) is now reported whatever the level; with level: error the warning used to filter itself out

devkit update no longer stops with an error from `go mod tidy` when a service still uses the log package that devkit-common v0.3.0 removed: it skips that step, says why, and goes on to show the steps below. 0.6.0 stopped before it could show them
action:
If your code still imports "<common>/log", move it to zlog, then finish the update by hand:
replace the import "<common>/log" with "<common>/zlog"
log.FromContext(ctx).Info("ping", "message", m)   ->   zlog.Ctx(ctx).Info("ping", zlog.Str("message", m))
go mod tidy && go build ./... && go vet ./...

changes: devkit-common v0.3.0: new logger zlog (on zap) replaces the log package. Console output for people: a color per level, file:line that GoLand and terminals turn into a link, key=value fields, stacks of errors and panics below the record with every frame a link. JSON output for collectors: service, env, host, version and the trace_id of the request on every record, never the same key twice
a trace_id follows a request from service to service (kitexx.ClientOptions now uses the TTHeader transport); zlog.Ctx(ctx) is the logger of the request
what Kitex and dependencies log (klog, log, log/slog) comes out in the same format
new log settings: format, stacktrace, max_field_bytes, sampling, buffer, version; log_level_data_id makes the level follow a Nacos configuration at run time
a service that cannot read its configuration now reports it through the logger; the Dockerfile sets ZLOG_FORMAT=json so that this line is JSON too
action:
The log package is gone from devkit-common, so handler code has to move to zlog. Replace the import "<common>/log" with "<common>/zlog" and rewrite the calls:
log.FromContext(ctx).Info("ping", "message", m)   ->   zlog.Ctx(ctx).Info("ping", zlog.Str("message", m))
slog.Error("save failed", "err", err)             ->   zlog.Error("save failed", zlog.Err(err))
Fields: zlog.Str, Int, Float, Bool, Dur, Time, Err, Any, Secret. go vet ./... finds what is left.
In conf/*.yaml replace `json: false` with `format: console` and `json: true` with `format: json`. The old key still works, so nothing breaks if you wait.
Clients made with kitexx.ClientOptions now speak TTHeader. Kitex servers accept it without any change; only a server that is not Kitex needs a look.

changes: devkit-common v0.2.1: when Nacos cannot be reached the service stops at once and names the address, the reason and the setting to check, instead of "client not connected, current status:STARTING" after a few seconds; it also explains a closed gRPC port (main port + 1000)
one Kitex version for the whole team: devkit update now also aligns the Kitex library in go.mod with the template, not only the generator version in the Makefile
make gen stops with a clear message when the installed kitex or thriftgo is not the team's version, instead of generating different code
versions can no longer be chosen per service or per project (needs devkit 0.1.9 or newer)
Dockerfile and GitLab CI use the Go release the common library needs (GoVersion, 1.26); with golang:1.24 the image refused to build because devkit-common requires Go 1.26
action:
If `make gen` now reports another kitex or thriftgo version, run:
make tools
If devkit.yaml has KitexVersion, ThriftgoVersion or CommonVersion under `vars:`, remove those lines; devkit 0.1.9 refuses them.

changes: library and tool versions (KitexVersion, ThriftgoVersion, CommonVersion) now follow the template on update instead of staying at the value from when the service was created; needs devkit 0.1.8 or newer
action:
Only if you want a service to stay on a specific version, pin it:
devkit update --set KitexVersion=v0.16.3

changes: new app/app.go, a file you own: the service's Config struct, a Setup function for its dependencies and shutdown cleanup, and optional extra server options
cmd/<service>/main.go is now pure framework code that calls app.Setup; nothing service-specific lives in it any more, so it can always be updated
action:
If you had edited cmd/<service>/main.go, it was left alone and the new version is next to it as main.go.new. Move your changes into app/app.go, then take the new file:
Config fields            -> the Config struct in app/app.go
kitexx.OnShutdown(...)   -> app.Setup
extra server options     -> app.ServerOptions
mv cmd/<service>/main.go.new cmd/<service>/main.go
If your handler needs dependencies, create them in app.Setup and pass them to handler.New(...).

changes: conf/README.md: a managed reference of every configuration setting, kept up to date by devkit update
new services get conf/dev.yaml and conf/prod.yaml with a detailed English/Chinese comment on every setting
action:
Your existing conf/*.yaml were not touched. For the explanations, read conf/README.md,
or create a scratch service with `devkit ngs` and copy the commented files from it.

changes: main.go: configuration is found from any start directory ($CONF_DIR, ./conf, next to the executable); start-up errors are plain messages instead of a panic
graceful stop: keeps serving after leaving Nacos, configurable drain time, kitexx.OnShutdown hooks that run after the last request
Kitex's internal logs use the same format as yours (logger=kitex); requires devkit-common v0.2.0, upgraded for you
action:
Optional, in each conf/<env>.yaml (defaults are 3s and 15s). Locally use deregister_wait: 0s so stopping is instant:
shutdown:
  deregister_wait: 3s
  drain_timeout: 15s

If the service owns resources, release them on shutdown. Since 0.4.0 this goes into app.Setup in app/app.go:
kitexx.OnShutdown("db", db.Close)

changes: the list of IDLs to generate moved from the Makefile to idl.mk, a file you own, so the Makefile can keep being updated
action:
If you had added IDLs to the IDLS line of the Makefile, put them into idl.mk:
IDLS := <service>/<service>.thrift other/other.thrift

changes: CI for GitLab (.gitlab-ci.yml) next to GitHub Actions; which one is generated follows where the code is hosted
action: If both files were generated and you only need one: devkit update --force --set CI=gitlab   (or github)
